purpose: Exploratory check of whether archived HMMA advice transfers across selected profiles; not an equal-budget search.

measurement.scope: public-full with preallocated buffers; per-call transforms and state copy included

correctness.optimized_hmma: bitwise-equal output and final state to official in all tested cases
correctness.cake_historical_peer: all three cases pass torch.testing.assert_close(atol=1e-2, rtol=1e-2)

interpretation: The optimized HMMA baseline is material: on H12 fixed8192 it closes a large part of the official-to-CAKE gap, while CAKE remains 1.53x faster under the historical peer contract.
The V16 recommendation is profile-scoped: forcing it on packed8x1024 or H96 fixed8192 is roughly 1.94x and 2.22x slower than auto respectively.
Numerical contract identity changes candidate admissibility; the historical peer contract and the newly introduced strict normalized-1pct contract must not be conflated.
The experiment supports scoped-memory organization but does not measure whether that organization improves agent search, nor does it provide equal-budget HMMA-vs-tcgen05 optimization.
limitations: Only three previously known profiles were tested.
Only nonzero BF16 initial state was tested.
Correctness is a peer comparison against official, not a new FP64 oracle.
The two contracts ran in separate allocations and absolute times must not be pooled across jobs.
Bootstrap intervals resample four paired block medians and quantify execution variability only.
